..
As of 209 PM EST Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A long stretch of mainly sunny and unseasonably
warm days will continue through the weekend. See Climate
section for some additional information. While we are seeing 
clear skies this afternoon areawide, upstream are some streaks 
of high altitude clouds ahead of a well-defined trough 
currently over Lake Superior. A smaller area of more widespread
cloudiness and some showers in the core of this trough will 
press eastward, passing to our north tonight such that we stay 
mostly clear. As such, it still looks like the only impact to 
our area will be increasing south- southwest winds tonight. The 
latest model data has backed off on the strength of the low 
level jet, with magnitudes more in the 30 to 40 knot range, with
resulting surface winds gusty primarily in the US 11 corridor 
in northern New York. As these winds back to the west and more 
widely mix to the surface after sunrise tomorrow, they will 
weaken resulting in only modest winds gusting to around 20 MPH 
and then backing off generally during the afternoon as high 
pressure builds back in. 

With high pressure moving to our east over the weekend, we'll
see more typical southerly flow and unseasonable warmth (925 
millibar temperatures near the 90th percentile in the 
climatology), especially given likely lack of cloud cover during
the daytime. Note both sky cover and potential for rain 
incoming as soon as Sunday afternoon is highly uncertain, 
especially in southern areas, pending the track of an expected 
coastal low to our south and discussed in the Key Message 2. 
High temperatures are unlikely to be affected but PoPs could 
trend higher for this timeframe.

KEY MESSAGE 2: An area of low pressure, currently under investigation 
by NHC, will work its way up the coast this weekend. The latest 
physics and AI based weather models are coming into agreement that 
we will see widespread rainfall overspread the region late Sunday 
and continue into Monday afternoon. Models are struggling to depict 
the actual low track but the latest runs are indicating that 1-2 
inches of rain, maybe even localized up to 3 inches, may be possible 
during this timeframe. There will likely be a sharp north to south 
gradient in precipitation amounts, similar to that of a Nor'easter, 
with the heaviest rain likely to occur across southern Vermont. The 
rainfall rates don't appear to be anything excessive at this time 
with rates likely a quarter of an inch per hour or less. We have 
seen drought conditions develop across the region over the past 45 
days due to the lack of any appreciable rainfall so this will be 
some welcomed and much needed rainfall. By Monday evening, rain 
appears like it'll taper off with rainfall building in behind. A 
sharp cold front will push through in the wake of the front with 
temperatures plummeting quickly following sunset.

KEY MESSAGE 3: There is very good agreement amongst the ensemble, 
deterministic, and AI based models that high pressure will remain 
large and in charge Tuesday and Wednesday. This will allow for good 
weather across the region for those looking to travel for 
Thanksgiving. The forecast for Thursday, on the other hand, is 
looking much trickier. Amongst all the guidance, we are seeing a 
bimodal distribution in forecast output with one option favoring 
strong (1040 mb+) high pressure over the region while the other 
shows a potent Nor'easter/coastal low pressure system. There appear 
to be two big players in play with one being the aforementioned high 
pressure system and another a yet to develop low pressure system off 
of Florida. The track of the strong high pressure system could 
largely impact the track of the low as a southern track of the high 
over Vermont will keep the low well south and offshore while a 
northern track north of Montreal would allow for this low to move 
further north. This could have significant travel implications later 
Thursday and on Friday or it could be a beautiful end of the week. 
Stay tuned as we will provide more information as it becomes 
available.
